### 📓 Docs Drift Check
**9** anchor(s) derived from **4** changed package(s); no hand-written page names any of them, so this run has **nothing to list** — **not a clean bill of health**. This check sees only pages that NAME a derived anchor: one that documents this change in prose, or enumerates it in an authoring dialect, names none and stays invisible to it on every run.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- **3** name(s) were too generic to anchor anything (single lowercase words)
- the SDK route bridge reached **65** of **247** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **182** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **182**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **59** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **123** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **179** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 68972cd29c55470a52c64d3366c2e5ef5cc25e8f` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `99138d202b35e6a205f70460c82147b504d5ad92` — the merge of head `5d3a6c757c49d4696db84da62689b37c2ac4f92f` into base `68972cd29c55470a52c64d3366c2e5ef5cc25e8f`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin 99138d202b35e6a205f70460c82147b504d5ad92 && git checkout 99138d202b35e6a205f70460c82147b504d5ad92
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin 68972cd29c55470a52c64d3366c2e5ef5cc25e8f 5d3a6c757c49d4696db84da62689b37c2ac4f92f && git checkout -B drift-repro 68972cd29c55470a52c64d3366c2e5ef5cc25e8f && git merge --no-ff 5d3a6c757c49d4696db84da62689b37c2ac4f92f

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 68972cd29c55470a52c64d3366c2e5ef5cc25e8f
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

Contract review and epic red-line read of card #32607, read at 2026-11-14T00:46Z. Inputs: the card and its rulings (6820653691, 6821134180, 6836791341), the diff of this head against merge base `89d7bef0`, the PR title and body, report 6868555489, the check-runs on this head, knock 6868544976. Claim 6868561553. Every finding below is by reading; nothing was run here.

### ① Derived judgments

- The declaration lines are present and of the right kind: `Clause-②: yes (narrowing)`, `Metadata-protocol: narrowed`, `Skills-docs: none`, the BREAKING banner, the `!` title, `adr-0087: registered` with the semantic entry. A read that served and now refuses is `narrowed`, as declared.
- `Skills-docs: none` holds by this seat's own reading. No skill and no docs page teaches the row saved first. The pages that speak of a name two packages hold (import-mappings.mdx, analytics.mdx, permission-sets.mdx) already teach the refusal naming each, so the read now agrees with them. The lifecycle page's bullet on a dependent's added locale teaches a base that ships, which the guard keeps.
- The FROM and TO table is right for the shape the pins cover: two enabled packages, one row each of one name at one member, no shipper, a type that is no bundle.
- Two "not moved" sentences do not hold as written, by reading: "pair rows make no holder" (M1) and "`/layers` keeps the package-less writes' refusal" together with the bundled-type row of the table (M2).

### ② Semver level

- Right: `minor` on `@objectstack/metadata-protocol`, `patch` on `@objectstack/rest`, `@objectstack/runtime` and `@objectstack/spec`.

### ③ Boundary flags

- Check-runs on this head at the time of reading: 64 runs, 26 success, 11 skipped, 27 in progress (Test Core 8 shards, Test UI 16 shards, three type checks), none failed. `Check Changeset` and the PR-body guards are green. The verdict below is FAIL, which does not wait for them.
- CI skipped the dogfood shards on this head (the gate job concluded in half a minute, its matrix skipped). The battery reading (462 files passed) is the report's.
- Order. Merge base `89d7bef0`; `main` is at `1169d64f`, twelve commits past it. None is on a path of this diff; #33149 and #33119 add other files beside the new semantic entry. A `git merge-tree` of `main` and this head reports no conflict.
- `Fixes #32607` closes a card whose sub-issue #32663 is open (the writer's registry keeps one bare slot per stored name). That card changes the registry holder set this judgment unions with the rows, so M1 and M2 read differently once it lands. The seat's to sequence.
- Residual left open by the declaration, no carrier named: a package-less row beside the rows of two packages returns the read "as it was" (`rows.unbound`), so the plain read still takes a row by store order while `/layers` refuses naming both. It is the card's own symptom on a neighbouring shape. The seat's to route.
- The row judgment's union and its pair filter also serve the arm #32354 landed for a disabled holder. M1's reading reaches that arm on `main` too; that part is not this diff's.

### ④ Design judgment

Red-line 1 read of the guard `abd91aad9e` (asked in the knock). It does not loosen resolution. The guard sits inside the arm this PR adds (no disabled holder), which `main` answered `undefined` without exception, and it returns that same `undefined`. It counts shippers as `packagelessContentPackage` counts them, at any member. No read `main` refused is served through it.

`servedRowHolderOf`, the new arm. The served set is the registry's holders of the name united with the packages the active rows are bound to at the member. With no shipper the registry knows a row-only name through one bare slot per member, the row written or hydrated last, while the rows name every package. The two sets are read at different grains (the name, and the member) and from different sources (one slot, and every row). The pinned shape is the one where that does not matter. M1 and M2 are two where it does.

The hand-over in both transports (`isItemOfDisabledPackage`) catches whatever the plain read throws and asks only whether step 1c has a refusal for the address. See S1.

The item face now reads the name's active rows once more on every read naming no package of a by-package type that no enabled package ships at the member and that has no environment item. See S2.

Findings:

- **M1 must-fix. A pair's row beside a row-held name is counted as a second holder in one save order.** Shape: package X stores a row of `d`, X's customization pair stores an undeclared row of `d`, no package ships `d`, nothing is disabled, any by-package type. When X's row is the bare slot's entry, the registry's holders are X, `pairsOf(X)` names the pair, the pair's row is filtered, one holder remains and the read is `main`'s. When the pair's row is the entry, `overlaySlotBinding` binds it to the pair itself (no composite holder for the pair to be a pair of), the registry's holders are the pair alone, `pairsOf` of a pair is empty, neither row is filtered, and the read is refused 409 naming X and its own pair. So the answer follows which row was saved last, and a pair is named as a holder, against the docblock's own rule and the changeset's "pair rows make no holder". Asked: a pin of this shape in both save orders, before and after a reboot, on the plain read, `/published` and the execution face, showing one answer and no refusal naming a pair; and the judgment made to agree with it. If the pin is green at this head as written, post the reading and M1 is withdrawn.
- **M2 must-fix. A dependent's added member over a row-held base is refused naming the base and the dependent, and `/layers` moves with it.** Shape: `email_template`; base A stores `en-US` of a name nobody ships; D, which declares A, stores `fr-FR`. The registry holds A alone (D is a bundle addition, #28802). The rows at `fr-FR` name D. The union is two, so the read at `fr-FR` naming no package is refused 409 naming A and D, where #28802 says an addition is no second holder of the name. On `main` that read served D's row (`packagelessContentPackage` with no shipper takes the row's own binding). `/layers` at `fr-FR` was not refused on `main` and is refused 409 here: the owner step's read throws, step 1c has no refusal for one candidate, and the error is rethrown. The guard closes this only for a base that ships in code. Asked: the same pin on the plain read, `/layers`, `/published` and the execution face at the added member, and the holders judged at one grain. I did not read the write gate: if it refuses D's row over a row-held base, post that refusal and M2 is withdrawn.
- **S1 should-fix. The hand-over does not look at what it caught.** For a name two packages ship in code, each with its own bound overlay row, the owner step's read throws the registry's refusal (as on `main`), step 1c has a refusal for two bound rows, and `/layers` now leads with the writes' sentence where it led with the plain read's. The A1 CONTROL pins two code holders with no rows, so it does not reach this. Either hand over only the refusal the row judgment made, or declare this row and pin it. The comment "every other refusal is rethrown" is true of neither.
- **S2 should-fix. One more store round trip on the hot path.** `host.readItemActiveRows(type, name)` in `servedRowHolderOf` is the uncached read; `readMetaItem` then reads the same rows through the overlay cache. Before this PR the row read was skipped unless some package was disabled. It now runs on every execution-face read of a Studio-authored flow, tool, skill or agent, and on every miss. Share the read with `readMetaItem`, or take it through the cache as that read does.
- **n1 nit.** No pin covers a bundled type or a member other than the canonical one; every new pin is a `dashboard`. M2's pin would be the first.
